name: Authorization Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in authorization work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in authorization work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer explicit, readable authorization solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
2. Document any non-obvious authorization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. Prefer the simplest authorization approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Validate authorization outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to authorization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Keep authorization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Check that authorization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting authorization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of authorization correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated authorization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new authorization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these authorization guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
